questions.stem: Drug X produces 50% of its effect at 1 mg and plateaus at 60% of the maximal tissue response. Drug Y produces 50% of its effect at 10 mg and plateaus at 100%. Which statement is correct?

options.A: X is more potent and more efficacious
options.B: X is more potent; Y is more efficacious
options.C: Y is more potent; X is more efficacious
options.D: Y is more potent and more efficacious
options.E: The two drugs have equal efficacy

questions.explanation: Potency = the dose needed for an effect (X needs less, so it's more potent); efficacy = the maximal effect regardless of dose (Y reaches the higher plateau). A: X's plateau is lower, so it's less efficacious. C: Reverses both properties. D: Y needs a 10× higher dose, so it's less potent. E: The plateaus differ (60% vs 100%).

questions.stem: Propranolol, a beta-blocker, blunts the heart's response to a beta-agonist but triggers no receptor response on its own. In terms of the two receptor properties, propranolol has:
questions.explanation: An antagonist has affinity (it binds, so it can block the agonist) but no intrinsic activity (binding triggers nothing). A: Affinity plus full intrinsic activity is a full agonist (e.g., beta-agonists). B: Partial intrinsic activity is a partial agonist, which would itself produce a submaximal response. C: A drug can't trigger a response without binding first. D: Without affinity it couldn't occupy the receptor and block the agonist.

questions.stem: A new antihypertensive lowers blood pressure markedly in a tightly controlled randomized trial. In routine clinics, its effect is much smaller because patients skip doses and have multiple comorbidities. Which pair of terms describes the trial result and the clinic result?
questions.explanation: Efficacy = whether a drug can work under ideal trial conditions; effectiveness = whether it does work in the real world. B: Potency is the dose needed for an effect, not trial vs real-world performance. C: Reverses the two. D: Cost-effectiveness is value for money (e.g., QALYs). E: Affinity and intrinsic activity are receptor properties.

questions.stem: In the 7-step therapeutic plan, a physician has just chosen the optimal plan for a 70-year-old woman with pneumonia. Which step comes next?
questions.explanation: The order is problem identification → desired outcome → therapeutic tools → therapeutic alternatives → optimal plan → outcome evaluation → patient education. A: Step 1. B: Step 2. D: Step 4, before the plan is chosen. E: Step 3.

questions.stem: A partial agonist is given at a concentration high enough to occupy all of its receptors. Which response is expected?

options.A: Zero response, because it blocks the receptor
options.C: A response above the full agonist's Emax
options.D: A submaximal response, below the full agonist's Emax
options.E: A full response, but only at a higher dose than the full agonist

questions.explanation: Partial agonists can't achieve full Emax even at saturating concentrations. A: Zero response at full occupancy describes an antagonist. B: 100% Emax is a full agonist. C: No agonist exceeds the system's maximal response. E: Needing a higher dose for the same maximum describes lower potency, not partial agonism.

questions.stem: Drug P is a partial agonist and drug F a full agonist at the same receptor. Both produce half of their own maximal effect at 1 mg. Which statement is correct?

options.A: P and F are equally potent, but P is less efficacious
options.B: P is less potent and less efficacious than F
options.C: P and F are equally efficacious, but P is less potent
options.D: P is more potent than F because it reaches its plateau sooner
options.E: P has no intrinsic activity, so it is an antagonist

questions.explanation: Potency is about the dose needed (same here); efficacy is the maximal effect, and a partial agonist can't reach full Emax even at saturating concentrations, yet it may appear equally potent. B: Equal doses for half-maximal effect mean equal potency. C: Reverses the two properties. D: Potency is judged by the dose for a given effect, not by when a lower plateau is reached. E: A partial agonist has some intrinsic activity; an antagonist has none.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man's blood pressure falls from 160/100 to 135/85 mmHg on metoprolol, a beta-blocker. A classmate says metoprolol has "0% efficacy" at the β-receptor. What best reconciles the two?

options.A: Metoprolol is a partial agonist with about 55% relative Emax
options.B: Metoprolol has no affinity for β-receptors; its effect isn't receptor-mediated
options.C: Zero molecular efficacy, yet clinically effective by blocking the receptor
options.D: It is efficacious only in trials; clinic results reflect effectiveness
options.E: It is highly potent, and potency replaces the need for efficacy

questions.explanation: An antagonist has 0% relative Emax at the molecular level but still "works" clinically; clinical and molecular definitions of efficacy differ. A: A partial agonist would itself stimulate the receptor; beta-blockers are antagonists. B: Antagonists have affinity; that's how they block. D: Efficacy vs effectiveness is about trial vs real-world conditions, not molecular vs clinical efficacy. E: Potency is the dose needed for an effect and doesn't explain zero intrinsic activity.
